verdict.rationale: First-party docs state that Edison maintains a "generous free tier for academics," with paid plans only for users who need higher rate limits or more features. That directly supports a researcher trying the product for free, using API keys self-served from the profile page. missing for 10: quantified free-tier limits (rate limits, task quotas, which agents such as Kosmos are included), clarity on eligibility for non-academic researchers, independent or hands-on confirmation that the free tier is meaningfully usable.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can try the product meaningfully on a free tier or trial

citations.quote: Edison maintains a generous free tier for academics. Researchers who need higher rate limits or additional features can subscribe to paid plans.
Edison maintains a generous free tier for academics.
Authentication is done by providing an API key, which can be obtained directly from your profile page in the Edison platform
